description: CO2 and TVOC exposure (see the related Air Quality entries for this mission) created a low-level health risk that was managed; crew remained alert to potential headaches as an early warning indicator throughout the mission.
response: Crew maintained daily monitoring; no headaches were reported. The vigilance itself may have contributed to early intervention.
lesson: The HSO should conduct a brief daily health check. CO2 and VOC levels are a shared crew responsibility — fatigue or headache must be reported immediately, not dismissed.
pattern_tag: air quality vigilance as early-warning practice
source_citation: SRC-hypatia-iii-brief, Part IV – Incident and emergency register, §4.5 Psychological and team dynamics, lines 758-763. Register Crew tag: 'C15'. Sol: not stated precisely; described as ongoing 'throughout the mission' — sol 1 used as onset. Confidence (B) rationale: daily-monitoring narrative; classified Near-Miss since no adverse health outcome (headache) actually occurred, distinct from the related Air Quality Failure entries for the same mission.
